correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact pair-midpoint identity H=m−∑a_i+2∑a_i|u_i|²−2|∑u_i|² and independently tested it on 900 random angle/coupling configurations with numerical discrepancies <1e−10. At fixed midpoint lengths, all nonzero vectors align by strict triangle inequality; minimization reduces to Q=∑a_i x_i²−(∑x_i)² over [0,1]^m. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz proves S≤1 minimizers, including equality x_i=t/a_i; for S>1 an admissible tiny vector makes Q<0, KKT one-sided derivatives force x_i=min(1,t/a_i), and F(t)=∑min(1/t,1/a_i) decreases strictly past min a to give one positive unique fixed point. Substitution yields E=m−∑a_i+2∑_{a_i≤t}(a_i−t); as S↓1 the root tends to min a. This proves the exact all-m integer and all-K>0 classification; numerical checks are only corroboration.

value.rationale: A natural, exactly solvable frustrated spin network has a collective transition controlled by the harmonic-like sum of heterogeneous antiferromagnetic bonds, rather than any individual bond. The full ground-state manifold and explicit jump quantify the frustration/ordering boundary, distinguishing a finite-system zero-temperature switch from a thermodynamic phase transition.
